assessment: The incumbent preassembles rearrangeable parts and checks an order slip, plausibly exposing fit and contents errors before dispatch; effectiveness is unmeasured. Its 11-minute median exceeds the target, five reports suggest contents failures without establishing all five independently, and seven of ten observed customers succeeded unaided. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes: a concrete limit on any claim that preassembly necessarily prevents meeting eight minutes. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching remain confounded. Overlapping widths in first-attempt and retried insertions also limit a width-only account. No supplied observation establishes one cause or validates a remedy.

openings.claim: Order switching during selection and checking may contribute to mixed-batch delays and incorrect partitions; complete order-specific staging may reduce both.
openings.delta: Retain preassembly while staging one complete order on a reusable marked board area before insertion.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout and worker, staging reduces selection/checking time and contents discrepancies; insertion time remains similar. If only six-compartment insertion stays slow, complexity better explains delays.
openings.probe: Use reversible sample builds, balancing worker, layout and condition order. Compare open-bin work with staged work; time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, including staging overhead. Independently reconcile components against each order. Screen within spare-board and available-time limits.
assumptions: Existing geometry, assortment, removable joints, ordered counts and colors remain intact.
Reusable staging stays within 500 initially and 0.40 per order; testing fits delivery slack.

openings.claim: With contents independently verified, does an order-specific slot map resolve uncertainty about the short partition?
openings.delta: Separate instruction ambiguity from actual missing or incorrect contents.
openings.prediction: Fewer placement questions and more unaided successes with the specific map support an instruction contribution; persistent difficulty points toward fit or placement ambiguity beyond the diagram.
openings.probe: Assign ten participants across generic versus order-specific diagrams with matched layouts and verified kits. Record unaided arrangement success and short-partition questions. Treat this small comparison as screening, not proof of the 90% target.
assumptions: Replacement diagrams meet the cost ceiling and delivery date.
Supplied components and ordered configurations remain unchanged.
